2. The present respondent as writ petitioner challenged a Memo dated 1.3.95 passed by appellant No. 2 requesting appellant No. 3 to withhold payment of Tk. 28 lakhs and odd from the pending bills of the present respondent. The respondent-company was issued an work order to construct six storied Bangladesh Bank Annexed Building at. Khulna. After substantial progress of work the respondent suffered as the work was hindered due to delay and laches of the Bangladesh Bank. The respondent prayed for price escalation and prayed for extension of time. Bangladesh Bank granted price escalation on certain conditions which the respondent did not accept. The respondent filed an application under Section 20 of the Arbitration Act for settlement of the dispute. A sole Arbitrator on hearing the parties passed an award on 21.5.94 After receipt of the said award money the respondent resumed the unfinished work and made substantial progress in the work. Thereafter the said award was made rule of the Court on 30.7.94 and the decree was signed and sealed on 3.8.94 In the meanwhile appellant No. 3 General Manager (Engineering Department). Bangladesh Bank wrote a Memo to appellant No. 2 on 1.8.94 wherein it was stated that an amount of Tk. 28 lakhs and odd has been awarded in excess by the sole Arbitrator which need to be recovered from the respondent from the Bills of the respondent. Hence appellant No. 2 issued the aforesaid Memo dated 1.3.95 which was impugned in the writ petition. 

 5. The learned Judges of the High Court Division made the Rule absolute mainly on the ground that the appellants arc not authorised to claim the aforesaid amount of Tk. 28 lakhs and odd without modification of the decree as well as modification of the Award. 

 1. The respondent having given an undertaking while receiving the award money from the appellants to refund excess payment made if any mistake is detected in the calculation in the award in future and the respondent not having denied the assertion made by the appellants in the affidavit-in-opposition to the effect that an amount of Tk. 80.40,000.00 was paid by the Bank for the supply of rod arid cement to the contractor as per clause 46 of the Tender document and that the value of work executed after 1.7.89 was taken for the purpose of the award as Tk. 79,61,103.12 instead of Tk. 75.95.072.92 and because of such mistake an amount of Tk. 28.24,288.76 was paid in excess, the High Court. Division erred in making the Rule absolute on the untenable view that the appellants were not competent to deduct such amount without modification of the award and the decree. 

 7. In this case Award was passed by the sole arbitrator on 21.5.94 and the award money was withdrawn by the present respondent on 2.6.94 by giving an undertaking (Ekrarnama) that the respondent would refund excess payment made to him if mistake is detected in calculation in future. Thereafter the award was made rule of the Court on 30.6.94 and decree was signed and scaled on 3.8.94. Subsequent thereto, after payment of the award money General Manager (Engineering Department) by his letter dated 1.8.94 addressed to appellant No. 2 clearly stated that as per clause 46 of the tender paper the Bank officer at Khulna supplied rod and cement of Tk. 80.40.000.00 which was also wrongly included in the award which the contractor is not entitled to get in view of this appellant No. 2 issued a memo dated I .3.95 (impugned in the writ petition) to with hold payment of Tk. 28 lakhs and odd from the pending bills. 

 This statement of the appellant in affidavit-in-opposition remained uncontroverted by the respondent. Consequently the fact of overpayment remains uncontroverted. It is apparent that the money was taken soon after the passing of the award on furnishing Ekrarnarna. The impugned memo was an internal communication to keep the disputed amount suspended. Hence it is not correct to say that without modification or amendment of the decree and the award, the letter of suspension of the amount could not be written. As a matter of fact the challenge of this letter is pre-mature as nothing was communicated to the respondent on the basis of the memo in question. The High Court Division raised the question of modification of the award and decree but the impugned memo before the High Court Division was relating to suspension of the payment till final adjudication of the matter. The learned Judges of the High Court Division primarily made the Rule absolute only on this untenable ground that the decree needs modification and amendment. We are afraid such view is not tenable legally in the facts of the present case when the undertaking was liven at the time of receiving the award money soon after passing of the award. Flintier disputed questions of calculations of claim and counter-claim cannot be decided in writ jurisdiction.
